Phrases chosen by key or by range

Source: R/phrases.R
lookup.Rd

lookup() builds a function from a named character vector (rule 3.3.2): the function takes a string or a factor (by label, never by integer code) and stops with a weft_value_error on a key it does not hold. brk() builds a function from formulas, tried in order (rule 3.3.3): brk(. < 0.95 ~ "a fall in", . <= 1.05 ~ "steady", TRUE ~ "a rise in"). A value no formula takes is a weft_value_error. Both functions vectorise, and given NA they stop with a weft_no_value error and never fall through to a default phrase (rule 3.3.5).

Usage

lookup(map)

brk(...)

Arguments

map

A named character vector: key to phrase.

...

Formulas whose left side is a condition on . and whose right side is the phrase.

Value

A function of one argument.

Examples

tier <- lookup(c(hi = "high", lo = "low"))
tier("hi")
#> [1] "high"
trend <- brk(. < 0.95 ~ "a fall in", . <= 1.05 ~ "steady", TRUE ~ "a rise in")
trend(c(0.9, 1, 2))
#> [1] "a fall in" "steady"    "a rise in"
